notes: The San Francisco Call's daily Building Contracts list for 1913, as far as the batches hold it: curiv_dardanelle_ver01 (1-15 February) and curiv_grimes_ver01 (16 July-8 December), 147 issues, 2,895 OCR pages. Located by the 1911-1912 two passes - the list's heading, mangled by the OCR ('Ralidtng Contracts', 'Bnildta* ©■tract*', 'Hnlldinx Contracts'), matched by its shape on a short line rather than its spelling, and the entry's own shape ('with CONTRACTOR - WORK ... line/corner of ...; $AMOUNT') - then a third pass over the full untrimmed spans for contract paragraphs: the 1912 trim at the first long gap between amounts dropped whole sub-lists in 1913, where the column is split around railway timetables, steamship notices and advertisements, and that pass recovered 27 entries, among them the Carpenters' Hall and Maritime Hall contracts and the second half of seven cut-off entries. Each block read by hand into structured fields. A contract reprinted later is kept once, at its first printing; private owners, trustees, guardianship estates and partnerships of surnames are cut from raw and extra; institutional and company owners are kept in extra.owner_firm; a notable owner the existing page already names (James L. Flood) is kept in extra.owner_notable_as_printed. A contractor's name garbled in one entry is corrected only where another entry prints it legibly (Devencenzi Bros., F. G. Denke, John Sparge, the Dairy Delivery company). Every entry carries extra.record_date. Placed with research/tools/corner.py --batch --json, which now checks the record's side of the street (or quadrant of the corner) against each candidate parcel's centroid and reports its distance from the crossing; a placement needs a single parcel matching the roll year within two years and, where the record gives them, the offset within 4 ft and the lot area within 4%, on the named side or in the named corner, storeys within one and a half, on the current roll. Corner records with no lot were judged by hand: the corner lot is the parcel addressed on both streets. Named buildings (the Palace of Fine Arts, the Exposition Auditorium, the Mills Building's Bush Street addition, the Palace Hotel, the Leesmont Apartments, St. Joseph's Church, the Flood residence) were placed on the building the record names. Pure renames applied for geometry only, as in 1912 (First avenue = Arguello, Army = Cesar Chavez, the lettered streets, Point Lobos avenue = Geary, Ocean boulevard = the Great Highway). One entry per building: the general contract, else the earliest, carries the page's entry, and an entry names only what its own cited issue prints.

coverage.remaining: Nothing of the 1913 lists the batches hold is known to remain unread. 1913's January, March to mid-July and 9-31 December are in no batch on the bulk route. The column did not run in the short 10-14 page issues of August-October (no Real Estate Transactions column at all), so 63 of the 147 issues have no list. 96 entries have no parcel matching the lot or offset with a roll year near 1913, 57 single candidates were refused (wrong side of the street, a roll year that does not fit, a retired parcel), 81 could not be measured, 17 are on the Panama-Pacific exposition grounds.
coverage.note: 2,895 OCR pages scanned; 103 page-blocks located by heading and shape, plus 27 entries recovered from the untrimmed spans; 385 contract entries read, 12 of them reprints and 4 fragments cut off with no location - 369 findings (309 building contracts, 60 alterations). 88 resolved - 81 by hand (64 by corner, offset and lot with corner.py's geometry, 17 on a building the record names) and 7 by a printed street number - and 281 unresolved: 96 with no parcel matching the lot or offset with a roll year near 1913, 57 single candidates refused, 81 not measurable (no cross street or offset, expunged streets such as Ecker, Oregon and Delaware, illegible names), 17 on the exposition grounds, 11 located only by a tract lot, 4 matching several parcels, and 15 others each with its reason (rebuilt parcels - the Academy of the Sacred Heart's corner, Holly Courts at 15 Patton - a condominium, printed numbers with no EAS record or a garbled digit, a number and an offset that disagree). 69 published on 68 pages, 46 of them seeded; 19 declined - 2 already on their pages from this source's 1913 real-estate pages, 15 further contracts for a building whose entry already carries one, 2 trade contracts that say nothing a reader needs.
